summary: The PR adds `[[Target|Label]]` support to wikilinks. The link text changes and the URL is still built from the target. Whitespace around the pipe is ignored, and `[[Page]]` behaves as before. The full suite passes and my own probes behaved as the issue asks.

own_checks.check: [[Target|Label]] gives the label as text and the target's URL
Whitespace around the pipe does not matter
own_checks.command: markdown.markdown('[[Getting Started | read the guide]]', extensions=['wikilinks'])
own_checks.output_excerpt: same output as the version without spaces

own_checks.check: base_url, end_url and html_class still apply to labelled links
Edge cases outside the PR's tests: empty label, extra pipes, mixed labelled and plain links, non-ASCII label
own_checks.output_excerpt: [[A|]] and [[A|B|C]] stay literal; mixed line renders two links; é label works

notes: A label containing characters outside the target charset, such as `.` or `*`, is not recognised and stays literal text (`[[A|b.c]]`). The docs say the label accepts the same characters as the target, so this is consistent with the documented behaviour.
`[[A|]]` with an empty label stays literal rather than falling back to the target text. This is a reasonable choice, and the issue does not cover it.
The `docs/changelog.md` entry is present, and the docs page was updated.
